Scholarships

blocks.label: Stage 1 — Foundation
blocks.text: Welding safety, metal preparation, engineering drawings and basic measurement.

blocks.label: Stage 2 — Process skills
blocks.text: ARC/SMAW, MIG/GMAW and TIG/GTAW welding; joint preparation and welding positions.

blocks.label: Stage 3 — Advanced practice
blocks.text: Welding parameters, distortion control, defect identification and inspection.

blocks.label: Stage 4 — Career preparation
blocks.text: Practical weld tests, workshop experience, apprenticeship applications and process-specific certification where required.

blocks.label: Practice projects
blocks.text: Butt joint • Fillet joint • Sheet-metal assembly • Pipe weld practice under supervised workshop conditions.

India’s DGT lists the general Welder trade as a one-year, 1,200-hour CTS course with Class 8 as the listed minimum entry qualification. The specialized Welder (GMAW & GTAW) trade is also listed as one year.

blocks.label: Government / public sector
blocks.text: Railway workshops, defence production units, public-sector engineering and fabrication facilities.

blocks.label: Private sector
blocks.text: Shipyards, automotive suppliers, construction and fabrication companies, industrial equipment manufacturers.

blocks.label: Ideal training areas
blocks.text: Structural welding • Pipe welding • TIG welding • MIG welding • Weld inspection.
Search Apprenticeship India for openings. Selection, stipend and eligibility depend on each employer’s notification.

blocks.label: Inspection route
blocks.text: Welding experience + suitable additional training → Welding Quality / Inspection Assistant.

blocks.label: Supervisory route
blocks.text: Experience + technical development → Welding Foreman / Fabrication Supervisor.

blocks.text: TIG stainless steel, MIG fabrication, pipe welding, structural steel, pressure equipment and robotic welding.

blocks.label: Industries
blocks.text: Automotive, construction, shipbuilding, oil and gas, power, heavy engineering, railways and industrial fabrication.

blocks.label: Technical skills
blocks.text: Joint preparation, welding positions, parameter control, weld defect recognition, drawing interpretation, material identification and safe work practices.

blocks.label: Equipment / tools
blocks.text: Welding power sources, electrodes, MIG wire feeders, TIG torches, clamps, gauges and PPE.
Useful credentials:

items.text: Process-specific welding qualification tests required by an employer or project.
Welding inspection training for relevant inspection roles.

blocks.text: Welding qualifications can be process-, material-, position- and application-specific. One certificate does not automatically qualify a person for every welding job.

blocks.label: Countries to explore
blocks.text: Germany, Canada, Australia, UK and New Zealand.

blocks.label: Training routes
blocks.text: Recognized vocational colleges and technical training providers offering welding, fabrication, metalworking or welding inspection programs.

blocks.label: Common requirements
blocks.text: Relevant prior education or trade experience, practical assessments, language proficiency where required, and study-visa documentation. Course availability and credential recognition vary by country.

blocks.label: Potential roles
blocks.text: Welder, TIG Welder, Pipe Welder, Fabricator and Welding Technician.

blocks.label: Industries
blocks.text: Shipbuilding, construction, energy, transport, heavy equipment and manufacturing.
